t: Minimum Partition Score — Convex Cost Partition DP
o: Split nums into exactly k contiguous subarrays minimizing the sum of f(s) = s(s+1)/2 over subarray sums s. Example 1: [5] and [1,2,1] gives 15+10=25. Example 2 with k=1 forces one piece worth 55. Example 3 with k=n forces all singletons. n ≤ 1000, so an O(n²k) DP is borderline; since f is convex, the classic divide-and-conquer optimization (monotone argmin) reduces this to O(nk log n).
k: Prefix sums turn each subarray value into f(pre[i]-pre[p]).
Because f is convex, splitting never hurts and the optimal split point is monotone across i — enabling D&C optimization.
dp[j][i] = min over p < i of dp[j-1][p] + f(pre[i]-pre[p]), answer dp[k][n].

a.n: Approach 1: Layered DP, O(n²) per layer
a.i: Straightforward transition: for each layer j and end i, try every possible previous boundary p.
s: For j = 1..k, for i = j..n, take min over p in [j-1, i-1] of dp[p] + f(pre[i]-pre[p]).
a.t: O(n²k) — three nested loops; fine for n = 1000 only in fast languages

a.i: For convex cost w(l,r) = f(sum), the argmin split point opt[j][i] is non-decreasing in i (quadrangle inequality). So each layer can be solved with the D&C trick: solve the middle index, then recurse left/right with narrowed opt ranges.
s: Same prefix sums and layered dp.
For each layer, call rec(range of i, range of candidate p).
At midpoint mid, linearly scan allowed p to find the best split bo.
Recurse on [lo, mid-1] with p-range [ol, bo] and [mid+1, hi] with [bo, oh].

c.python:
class Solution:
    def minimumPartitionScore(self, nums, k):
        n = len(nums)
        pre = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i, x in enumerate(nums): pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + x
        INF = float('inf')
        dp = [0] * (n + 1)
        for _ in range(k):
            nd = [INF] * (n + 1)
            def rec(lo, hi, ol, oh):
                if lo > hi: return
                mid = (lo + hi) // 2
                best, bo = INF, ol
                for p in range(ol, min(mid - 1, oh) + 1):
                    if dp[p] < INF:
                        s = pre[mid] - pre[p]
                        v = dp[p] + s * (s + 1) // 2
                        if v < best: best, bo = v, p
                nd[mid] = best
                rec(lo, mid - 1, ol, bo)
                rec(mid + 1, hi, bo, oh)
            rec(1, n, 0, n - 1)
            dp = nd
        return dp[n]

a.t: O(nk log n) — each layer's D&C does O(n log n) transitions total
a.sp: O(n) — DP rows plus recursion stack O(log n)

w: Present the plain DP first, then upgrade with D&C optimization after noting convexity (this also implies a monotone queue / SMAWK solution exists). Watch for overflow: scores reach ~5e13, so use 64-bit integers. Edge cases: k = 1 and k = n. Follow-up: prove why convexity gives the monotone argmin.
